arxiv-1908-07880.title: Universal Reconfiguration of Facet-Connected Modular Robots by Pivots: The O ⁡ ( 1 ) O(1) Musketeers
arxiv-1908-07880.creator: Hugo A. Akitaya, Esther M. Arkin, Mirela Damian, Erik D. Demaine, Vida Dujmović, Robin Flatland, Matias Korman, Belén Palop, Irene Parada, André van Renssen, Vera Sacristán
arxiv-1908-07880.description: Abstract We present the first universal reconfiguration algorithm for transforming a modular robot between any two facet-connected square-grid configurations using pivot moves. More precisely, we show that five extra “helper” modules (“musketeers”) suffice to reconfigure the remaining n n modules between any two given configurations.

arxiv-2212-12139.title: HiTSKT: A Hierarchical Transformer Model for Session-Aware Knowledge Tracing Journal: Knowledge-Based Systems
arxiv-2212-12139.creator: Fucai Ke, Weiqing Wang, Weicong Tan, Lan Du, Yuan Jin, Yujin Huang, Hongzhi Yin
arxiv-2212-12139.description: Abstract Knowledge tracing (KT) aims to leverage students’ learning histories to estimate their mastery levels on a set of pre-defined skills, based on which the corresponding future performance can be accurately predicted. As an important way of providing personalized experience for online education, KT has gained increased attention in recent years.

arxiv-2302-02792.title: Dealing With Non-stationarity in Decentralized Cooperative Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning via Multi-Timescale Learning
arxiv-2302-02792.creator: Hadi Nekoei, Akilesh Badrinaaraayanan, Amit Sinha, Mohammad Amini, Janarthanan Rajendran, Aditya Mahajan, Sarath Chandar
arxiv-2302-02792.description: Abstract Decentralized cooperative multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MARL) can be a versatile learning framework, particularly in scenarios where centralized training is either not possible or not practical. One of the critical challenges in decentralized deep MARL is the non-stationarity of the learning environment when multiple agents are learning concurrently.

arxiv-2303-06731.title: A note on the physical process first law of black hole mechanics
arxiv-2303-06731.creator: Antoine Rignon-Bret
arxiv-2303-06731.description: Abstract I give a simple proof of the physical process first law of black hole thermodynamics including charged black holes, in which all perturbations are computed on the horizon. 1 Introduction One of the most mysterious and promising topics in modern physics is the deep connection between the laws of black hole mechanics and the fundamental principles of thermodynamics.

arxiv-2305-18389.title: AnoRand: A Semi Supervised Deep Learning Anomaly Detection Method by Random Labeling
arxiv-2305-18389.creator: Mansour Zoubeirou A Mayaki, Michel Riveill
arxiv-2305-18389.description: Abstract Anomaly detection or more generally outliers detection is one of the most popular and challenging subject in theoretical and applied machine learning. The main challenge is that in general we have access to very few labeled data or no labels at all.

arxiv-2307-07750.title: Origin of Low- Al 26 / Al 27 {}^{26}{\rm Al}/{}^{27}{\rm Al} Corundum/Hibonite Inclusions in Meteorites
arxiv-2307-07750.creator: Steven J. Desch, Emilie T. Dunham, Ashley K. Herbst, Cayman T. Unterborn, Thomas Sharp, Maitrayee Bose, Prajkta Mane, Curtis D. Williams
arxiv-2307-07750.description: Abstract Most meteoritic calcium-rich, aluminum-rich inclusions (CAIs) formed from a reservoir with Al 26 / Al 27 ≈ 5 × 10 − 5 \mbox{${}^{26}{\rm Al}/{}^{27}{\rm Al}$}\approx 5\times 10^{-5} , but some record lower ( Al 26 / Al 27 ) 0 (\mbox{${}^{26}{\rm Al}/{}^{27}{\rm Al}$})_{0} , demanding they sampled a reservoir without live Al 26 {}^{26}{\rm Al} .

arxiv-2403-13635.title: Lattice Polaron in a Bose-Einstein Condensate of Hard-Core Bosons
arxiv-2403-13635.creator: Moroni Santiago-García, Shunashi G. Castillo-López, Arturo Camacho-Guardian
arxiv-2403-13635.description: Abstract Lattice polarons, quasiparticles arising from the interaction between an impurity and its surrounding bosonic environment confined to a lattice system, have emerged as a platform for generating complex few-body states, probing many-body phenomena, and addressing long-standing problems in physics.

arxiv-2407-01333.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Adverse Garage Scenario Generation
arxiv-2407-01333.creator: Kai Li
arxiv-2407-01333.description: Abstract Autonomous vehicles need to travel over 11 billion miles to ensure their safety. Therefore, the importance of simulation testing before real-world testing is self-evident. In recent years, the release of 3D simulators for autonomous driving, represented by Carla and CarSim, marks the transition of autonomous driving simulation testing environments from simple 2D overhead views to complex 3D models.

arxiv-2511-12647.title: Inverse determination of light–matter coupling in disordered systems from transmittance spectra
arxiv-2511-12647.creator: Thales F. Macedo, Julián Faúndez, Antônio S. Coelho, Caio Lewenkopf, Mauro S. Ferreira, Felipe A. Pinheiro, Natanael C. Costa
arxiv-2511-12647.description: Abstract We investigate quantum inverse problems in one-dimensional (1D) electronic disordered systems strongly coupled to optical cavities. More specifically, we consider the Anderson and the Aubry-Andre-Harper models connected to electronic researvoirs and embedded in a single-mode optical cavity. The light-matter interaction enables photon-assisted hopping processes that significantly modify the transmittance spectrum.

britannica-1911-tula-government.title: Tula (government) (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-tula-government.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-tula-government.description: Article 'Tula (government)' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 27), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. The government is divided into twelve districts, the chief towns of which are Tula, Bogoroditsk, Alexin, Byelev, Epifan, Efremov, Kashira, Krapivna, Novosil, Odoyev, Chern and Venev. Only 2.4% of the aggregate area is considered as unavailable for cultivation, the remainder being distributed as follows: peasants, 482%; nobility, 322%; other private landowners, 11%; crown, towns, &c., 2%.

plos-pone-0005543.title: Spatial Representations Are Specific to Different Domains of Knowledge
plos-pone-0005543.creator: Rowena Beecham, Robert A. Reeve, Sarah J. Wilson
plos-pone-0005543.description: PLOS ONE research article. There is evidence that many abstract concepts are represented cognitively in a spatial format. However, it is unknown whether similar spatial processes are employed in different knowledge domains, or whether individuals exhibit similar spatial profiles within and across domains.

pmc-10742374.title: Impact of bioenergy feedstock carbon farming on sustainable aviation fuel viability in the United States
pmc-10742374.creator: Sagar Gautam, Nawa Raj Baral, Umakant Mishra, Corinne D. Scown
pmc-10742374.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). SignificanceCultivation of deep-rooted biomass crops can simultaneously achieve atmospheric carbon removal via SOC sequestration while providing much-needed energy-dense fuels to the aviation sector. These two outcomes may be incentivized differently. Farmers may be paid for SOC sequestration based on crop choice and farming practices, while biojet fuel can be sold at a premium on a volumetric basis without considering soil carbon impacts. However, price premiums for biojet fuels and payments for SOC sequestration will incentivize different activities, depending on the relative value.

pmc-11314251.title: Antrodia camphorata Supplementation during Early Life Alters Gut Microbiota and Inhibits Young-Onset Intestinal Tumorigenesis in APC1638N Mice Later in Life
pmc-11314251.creator: Tingchun Lin, Lauren Daddi, Ying Tang, Yanjiao Zhou, Buping Liu, Matthew D. Moore, Zhenhua Liu
pmc-11314251.description: Young-onset colorectal cancer is an increasing concern worldwide due to the growing prevalence of Westernized lifestyles in childhood and adolescence. Environmental factors during early life, particularly early-life nutrition, significantly contribute to the increasing incidence. Recently, there have been reports of beneficial effects, including anti-inflammation and anti-cancer, of a unique fungus (Antrodia camphorate, AC) native to Taiwan.

pmc-11597883.title: An Electrochemical Biosensor Analysis of the Interaction of a Two-Vector Phospholipid Composition of Doxorubicin with dsDNA and Breast Cancer Cell Models In Vitro
pmc-11597883.creator: Lyubov V Kostryukova, Anastasia S Serdyukova, Veronica V Pronina, Victoria V Shumyantseva, Yulia A Tereshkina, Wei Wu, Sibusiso Alven, Blessing Atim Aderibigbe
pmc-11597883.description: Objectives: The main aim of our experiments was to demonstrate the suitability of cell-based biosensors for searching for new anticancer medicinal preparations. Methods: The effect of the substance doxorubicin, doxorubicin embedded in phospholipid nanoparticles, and doxorubicin with phospholipid nanoparticles modified by targeting vectors (cRGD and folic acid) on dsDNA and breast cancer cell lines (MCF-7, MDA-MB-231) was studied.

pmc-12422735.title: p53 isoforms have a high aggregation propensity, interact with chaperones and lack binding to p53 interaction partners
pmc-12422735.creator: Anamari Brdar, Christian Osterburg, Philipp Münick, Anne Christin Machel, Rajeshwari Rathore, Susanne Osterburg, Büşra Yüksel, Birgit Schäfer, Kristina Desch, Julian D Langer, Ivan Dikic, Volker Dötsch, Julien Roche, Anamari Brdar, Christian Osterburg, Philipp Münick, Anne Christin Machel, Rajeshwar
pmc-12422735.description: The p53 transcription factor family consists of the three members p53, p63, and p73. Both p63 and p73 exist in different isoforms that are well characterized. Isoforms have also been identified for p53 and it has been proposed that they are responsible for increased cancer metastasis.

pmc-12816004.title: The application of ABC-VED with multi-criteria analysis for drug inventory management
pmc-12816004.creator: Assefa Beyene Ayalew, Aschale Getnet Alemu, Alebachew Mengistu Worku
pmc-12816004.description: Effective drug inventory management is critical for ensuring the availability of essential medicines while minimizing costs and reducing wastages in healthcare institutions. This study presents a comprehensive approach that integrates Always Better Control (ABC) and Vital Essential Desirable (VED) analysis with multi criteria analysis to optimize pharmaceutical inventory control.

pmc-13260842.title: Cation design in complex aqueous electrolytes for low-temperature zinc-bromine flow batteries
pmc-13260842.creator: Tao Cheng, Ming Zhao, Tianyu Li, Shuo Wang, Yanbin Yin, Xianfeng Li
pmc-13260842.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The cation design of the multi-component dynamic concentration electrolytes that simultaneously achieve effective phase transition prevention and rapid kinetic process is challenging but vital for enhancing the performance of low-temperature zinc-bromine flow batteries. Herein, we employ NH4+ as supporting electrolyte cation to break inherent trade-off between salting-out at low temperatures and ion transport kinetic from the alkali cations (K+, Na+ and Li+).

pmc-13297040.title: Regime-Dependent Elastic Displacement in Bio-Inspired Parametric Kirigami Structures: An Experimental Study of Geometric Parameter Effects
pmc-13297040.creator: Tarek H. Mokhtar, Somaih M. Bakr, Qusai R. Khashman

pmc-13321657.title: Iba1 deficiency impairs microglial synaptic remodeling and neuronal survival after axonal injury
pmc-13321657.creator: Koji Sekiguchi, Hirotaka Shoji, Tomoko Shindo, Jumpei Sasabe, Daiki Tokuyasu, Jin Nakahara, Tsuyoshi Miyakawa, Daisuke Ito
pmc-13321657.description: BackgroundMicroglia remodel neuronal circuits in pathological conditions; however, the molecular requirements for these responses and their consequences for motoneuron survival remain unclear.MethodsAif1 (Iba1) knockout mice were generated using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated deletion, and baseline phenotypes and responses to unilateral facial nerve axotomy were assessed using immunohistochemistry, transmission electron microscopy, and single-nucleus RNA sequencing of the facial motor nucleus.

pmc-13616735.title: Expression of circulating GRP78 and gp96, endoplasmic reticulum stress-related proteins, in menstrual and bladder pain sensitivity
pmc-13616735.creator: Chandrashekara N. Kyathanahalli, Sarah E. Darnell, Frank F. Tu, Kevin M. Hellman
pmc-13616735.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Dysmenorrhea is often linked to uterine inflammation, but the additional factors and pathways that contribute to its pathophysiology remain poorly understood. Given growing evidence linking endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress to inflammation and pain sensitization, we examined circulating ER stress-associated heat shock proteins (HSPs) GRP78 and gp96 in individuals with dysmenorrhea (n = 82), a dysmenorrhea subtype with bladder pain sensitivity (DYSB, n = 26) previously shown to increase risk for chronic pain, and controls (n = 19).
